precepts.text: Mark adds the scribe's answer: to love God with all the heart and understanding and his neighbour as himself is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.
precepts.point: Whosoever shall keep the whole law and yet offend in one point is guilty of all: the Christian says you cannot keep them, but the context is the royal law, as the next verse shows, he that said do not commit adultery said also do not kill. Speak and do as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty, since Christ redeemed us from the death the moral law carried; he shall have judgment without mercy that hath showed no mercy.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Mark gives the same account with more detail, and it ties into sacrifice. “And one of the scribes came.” In Matthew he is called a lawyer; in Mark he is called a scribe, because they wrote things over and over and had the law in their minds. There were a bunch of them, but he was bold and spoke up: “Which is the first commandment of all?”

“The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord”: that is Deuteronomy 6:4. “And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment.” The commandments, the dietary law, the civil law, the sacrificial law, all of that is in there. “And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.” If you can keep those, you can keep them all.

“Well, Master, thou hast said the truth”: true, true, true. Then verse 33: “to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” It is better than sacrifices. That is why Mark is loved: he makes it clear.

Why is it more than sacrifices? Because Israel would mess around, offer sacrifices, and then hate their neighbour, kill their neighbour, steal from their neighbour, bang their neighbour’s wife or sleep with their neighbour’s husband, but offer the best animal. The Lord said, I don’t care about that stuff. I care about your obedience, loving each other, loving me above the animals.

precepts.text: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord; love him with all thy heart, soul, mind and strength; and love thy neighbour as thyself; there is none other commandment greater. Love your people, love your ways.
precepts.point: He that loveth his brother abideth in the light and there is none occasion of stumbling in him; he that hateth his brother walketh in darkness, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes. Hate of your brother blinds you to deep but basic scriptures.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Normally Matthew 22 is read for this, but Mark is heavy. A scribe asked, “Which is the first commandment of all?” “And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment. And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.”

There is none greater, because if you love your brother as yourself you can keep all the commandments; they all go hand in hand. You cannot love God and hate your brother. By loving God you will love your brother, and by loving your brother you love God.

What Christ is really saying is: love your people, love your ways. Why would the Most High give us these laws? Because we had learned how to hate one another, and the law was given to teach us. The same laws we give to our people today: love your ways, love your people, love your neighbour.

Think how brainwashed you are in this captivity if, like Deacon Nathan was saying earlier, you are in captivity and care more about your oppressor than your own kind. Your people are being oppressed and all you care about is your oppressor: you're a dummy, and that is the kindest word for it. That is the darkness that “hath blinded his eyes.”

precepts.text: The husbandmen killed the heir and cast him out, so the lord of the vineyard will destroy them; the stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner.
precepts.point: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner; this is the Lord's doing and it is marvelous in our eyes. This is prophecy speaking of Christ, showing that Christ is in the Old Testament.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. This is the Lord’s doing; it is marvellous in our eyes.” This is prophecy speaking of Christ, and Christ himself applies it. “But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours. And they took him, and killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.”

“What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.” Then Christ asks, “And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner: This was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?”

The heir the husbandmen killed and cast out is the stone the builders refused, and he is become the head of the corner. Christ is in the Old Testament, and he read this psalm of himself.

precepts.text: Boaz raises up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that his name be not cut off from among his brethren; that is what the law was for.
precepts.point: He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living.

note.label: Mark 12: The Husbandmen, the Tribute, and the First Commandment

precepts.why:
The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, build a question on the law Moses wrote: “If a man’s brother die, and leave his wife behind him, and leave no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.” Seven brethren, one wife, no seed; whose wife is she in the resurrection? “Do ye not therefore err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God?”

They did not know what that law was for. Boaz shows it: “Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place”. The law was for inheritance, so that a dead man's name and portion would not be put out of Israel. It has nothing to do with whose wife a woman is in the resurrection.

A woman is bound by that law while her husband lives, and “when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage”. In the resurrection there is no more dying, so there is no dead brother's name to raise up. “He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living”.

precepts.text: The commandment Christ was quoting, word for word out of the law.
precepts.point: The scribe answered discreetly, and was told, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God, and no man after that durst ask him any question.

note.label: Mark 12: The Husbandmen, the Tribute, and the First Commandment

precepts.why:
Asked which is the first commandment of all, Christ answered word for word out of the law: “Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.” The first of all the commandments is that the Lord our God is one Lord, and to love him with all thy heart, soul and strength.

Loving him is keeping his commandments. And the second is like it, “Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” Loving your neighbour as yourself means holding him to those commandments as you hold yourself, because the wages of sin is death and you do not want to see your brother die. “There is none other commandment greater than these.”

The scribe answered discreetly, that to love him and his neighbour “is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices”, and was told, “Thou art not far from the kingdom of God.” After that no man durst ask him any question.

precepts.text: The psalm quoted: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
precepts.point: Beware of the scribes, which love to go in long clothing, and love salutations in the marketplaces, and the chief seats in the synagogues. What they wanted was the recognition of men.

note.label: Mark 12: The Husbandmen, the Tribute, and the First Commandment

precepts.why:
“How say the scribes that Christ is the Son of David? For David himself said by the Holy Ghost, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool.” This is the psalm he quoted: “The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.”

David, by the Holy Ghost, calls Christ “my Lord”. “David therefore himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he then his son?” The scribes called Christ the son of David and stopped there; David himself called him Lord, seated at the right hand of the Lord until his enemies are made his footstool. The common people heard him gladly. The scribes, who loved long clothing, salutations in the marketplaces and the chief seats in the synagogues, wanted the recognition of men, and they missed what David saw.

precepts.text: He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.
precepts.point: The rich cast in much, but the poor widow threw in two mites, and he says she cast in more than they all, for they cast in of their abundance, but she of her want did cast in all that she had.

note.label: Mark 12: The Husbandmen, the Tribute, and the First Commandment

precepts.why:
The rich cast much into the treasury, and a poor widow threw in two mites. “Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.”

Paul lays down the rule: “He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.” The rich gave much and sowed sparingly, because it was out of their abundance; the widow gave two mites and sowed bountifully, because it was all she had. The measure is not the sum but what it cost the giver, and the reaping follows that.

note.label: Living Martyrs

precepts.why:
“All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.” That is what we read in Job 3 at the beginning of the lesson.

“Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward”: when your body is destroyed, taken down, your spirit goes up before the Lord. “And the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth”: the spirit of the beast stays down here. It doesn’t go up before the Lord.

Up before the Lord there are chambers, resting places, for you and me to go to, until the time comes when Christ says now it is time for heaven and hell, and takes the keys of hell and of death. Some will be raised up to everlasting life, and some to everlasting condemnation. That is why the Lord is the God of the living, and that is why we have to do right.

precepts.why:
“Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might entangle him in his talk. And they sent out unto him their disciples with the Herodians.” They asked, “Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not?” Is it lawful to pay taxes?

“But Jesus perceived their wickedness”, called for the tribute money, and asked, “Whose is this image and superscription?” “Render therefore unto Cesar the things which are Cesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.” They couldn’t catch Christ in his words about taxes, because he paid taxes. They knew that by not paying taxes, Rome could arrest you and execute you.

You have that going on today. People in the congregation in Oklahoma City said they were sovereign and didn’t have to pay taxes, and they lost their houses, their jobs, everything; without a social security card, a driver’s license or an identity, they get fired, and then they are upset with us. If you are getting rid of your birth certificate, social security, driver’s license and citizenship, you are an idiot. When they put you out of the country, what country can you go to with no passport?

Another group, blacks and Latinos, said no idols and no images, took a black marker to the dollar bill and blacked out the pyramid, the eye, the eagle, United States and George Washington’s face, then went to the store to pay with it and were thrown out. Some Israelites learn a little knowledge and exit stage left into stupidity.

He who has nothing to die for has nothing to live for. If you are not willing to die for this truth, you are not fit to live.
